post:
Energy-renovated flats are tight, and a wardrobe against a cold corner plus closed windows is a classic recipe for mould.

I built mould-risk-index, an open-source Python monitor for rental flats. Cheap temperature and humidity sensors feed a dew-point and wall-surface-humidity calculation (temperature factor fRsi), the VTT dynamic mould index, and an advice engine that writes plain recommendations in German, French, Italian and English. A weekly report stays neutral between tenant and landlord, and all data stays local. It includes a 7-byte BLE and LoRaWAN payload with a JavaScript decoder.

I simulated three behaviours in two building types over one winter with real hourly Zurich weather from Open-Meteo. In the tight flat the mould index reached 5.3 with bad habits and 0.02 with good airing. About 20 minutes of daily cross ventilation took days at index 1 or higher from 154 to 0, and a cold-corner sensor missed 0.06 events per flat-month against 0.47 for a room sensor with a generic assumption.

What is not verified: the indoor climate is simulated, and neither it nor the mould model was checked against a real flat or observed mould.

If you manage rental housing, would you want a tool that shows both the airing and the wall-temperature side?

Code: https://github.com/VB-Builds/mould-risk-index
